name: SU7000

resolution.note: 0.8 nm at 15 kV, 0.9 nm at 1 kV

specs.Detectors: Upper, middle and lower detectors standard; BSE, variable-pressure and STEM detectors optional

summary: A Schottky field-emission SEM with upper, middle and lower electron detectors as standard and optional backscatter, variable-pressure and STEM detectors. Hitachi sells it alongside the higher-resolution SU8700.

sources.title: Hitachi High-Tech Europe: SU7000 and SU8700 FE-SEM

name: TM4000Plus II

specs.Detectors: 4-segment BSE detector and low-vacuum SE detector (UVD)
specs.Sample size: up to 80 mm diameter, 50 mm thick
specs.Modes: BSE, SE and mixed images, with charge-up reduction

summary: A tabletop SEM that works at low vacuum, so non-conductive or hydrated samples can be looked at without coating. The Plus II adds a secondary-electron detector to the backscattered-electron detector of the base TM4000 II.

sources.title: Hitachi High-Tech Europe: TM4000 Series Tabletop SEM

name: CLARA

resolution.note: 0.7 nm at 15 keV; 1.0 nm at 1 keV; 1.1 nm at 500 eV

specs.Landing energy: 20 eV-30 keV (<20 eV with beam deceleration)
specs.Detectors: Everhart-Thornley, in-column energy-filtered multidetector, in-column axial detector; BSE, STEM and CL optional

summary: A Schottky field-emission SEM with a field-free BrightBeam column, built for sub-nanometre imaging at low landing energies. Its in-column multidetector is energy-filtered.

sources.title: TESCAN CLARA: Ultra-High-Resolution SEM

name: MIRA

resolution.note: 1.0 nm at 30 keV (in-beam SE); 1.2 nm at 30 kV; 1.8 nm at 1 keV with beam deceleration

specs.Landing energy: 200 eV-30 keV (<50 eV with beam deceleration)
specs.Detectors: Everhart-Thornley standard; in-beam SE and BSE, STEM, CL and gaseous SE detectors optional

summary: TESCAN's Schottky field-emission SEM, with probe currents up to 400 nA and optional in-beam, backscatter, STEM and cathodoluminescence detectors.

sources.title: TESCAN MIRA FEG SEM

name: VEGA

resolution.note: 3.0 nm at 30 keV; 8.0 nm at 3 keV

specs.Vacuum: MultiVac mode up to 500 Pa (N2 or H2O)

summary: A tungsten-filament SEM for routine imaging and analysis, with a variable-pressure mode (up to 500 Pa) for uncoated, non-conductive samples.

sources.title: TESCAN VEGA: Analytical SEM for Materials Research

name: Spectra 300

resolution.note: STEM resolution 50 pm at 300 kV; 125 pm at 30 kV (probe-corrected)

specs.Electron source: X-FEG (optional monochromator) or X-CFEG cold FEG
specs.Monochromator energy resolution: tunable from 1 eV to <0.2 eV (X-FEG Mono); <0.03 eV (UltiMono)
specs.STEM detectors: Panther 16-segment solid-state detectors; EMPAD for 4D STEM

summary: An aberration-corrected scanning/transmission electron microscope for atomic-resolution imaging and spectroscopy in materials science. It works over a wide voltage range, so beam-sensitive materials can be imaged at lower energies.

sources.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific: Spectra 300 (S)TEM

name: Talos F200X

resolution.note: HRTEM line resolution <=0.10 nm; STEM <=0.16 nm (X-FEG), <=0.14 nm (X-CFEG)

specs.Electron source: X-FEG or X-CFEG cold field emission gun

summary: A 200 kV-class S/TEM built for fast chemical mapping: four EDS detectors arranged around the sample collect X-rays efficiently, so elemental maps can be acquired quickly alongside STEM images.

sources.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific: Talos F200X (S)TEM

name: JSM-IT510 InTouchScope

resolution.note: 3.0 nm at 30 kV and 15.0 nm at 1.0 kV (high vacuum); 4.0 nm at 30 kV (low vacuum, BED)

specs.EDS: optional; standard on A and LA models

summary: A conventional SEM in JEOL's InTouchScope line with optional integrated EDS, for imaging and elemental analysis. Low-vacuum versions (10-650 Pa) image uncoated, non-conductive samples.

sources.title: JEOL: JSM-IT510 InTouchScope Scanning Electron Microscope

name: JEM-F200

resolution.note: TEM lattice resolution 0.1 nm; point resolution 0.19 nm (UHR pole piece); HAADF-STEM 0.14 nm with cold FEG, at 200 kV

summary: A multi-purpose 200 kV field-emission TEM/STEM for high-resolution imaging and analysis, available with a cold field-emission gun for a narrow energy spread.

sources.title: JEOL: JEM-F200 Multi-purpose Electron Microscope

name: EVO 10 / 15 / 25

specs.Emitter: LaB6 emitter offered for higher resolution and signal-to-noise
specs.Vacuum modes: high vacuum and variable pressure; extended pressure for hydrated samples

summary: A thermionic SEM family in three chamber sizes for routine imaging and analysis of large or uncoated samples, with variable-pressure modes for non-conductive and hydrated specimens.

sources.title: ZEISS EVO Scanning Electron Microscope

name: Dimension XR

specs.Platform: built on the Dimension Icon or FastScan AFM
specs.Modes: PeakForce Tapping, PeakForce QNM, AFM-nDMA, FASTForce Volume, PeakForce TUNA, PeakForce KPFM, DataCube, EC-AFM, PeakForce SECM

summary: A family of large-sample AFMs packaged for quantitative work: each configuration bundles the probe modes for one kind of measurement (mechanical, electrical or electrochemical properties) on top of Bruker's Icon or FastScan platform.

sources.title: Bruker: Bruker Launches New Dimension XR Family of Scanning Probe Microscopes (28 Nov 2018)
Bruker: Dimension XR SPM

name: FX40

specs.Probe exchange: automatic tip exchanger storing up to 8 pre-mounted probes
specs.Automation: automatic probe exchange and laser beam alignment; sample-view camera

summary: A small-sample AFM that automates set-up steps such as changing the probe and aligning the laser beam, with a tip changer holding eight probes.

sources.title: Park Systems: Park FX40 Small Sample AFM

name: OpenFlexure Delta Stage
manufacturer: OpenFlexure (University of Bath and University of Cambridge)

specs.Imaging modes shown: brightfield, epi-fluorescence, darkfield, Rheinberg, differential phase contrast

summary: A 3D-printed motorised microscope for research labs, built from the OpenFlexure project with a delta-geometry stage. Its modular optics let users switch between several contrast methods, and the design files are under an open licence.
applications: Malaria parasite imaging in blood smears

sources.title: Multi-modal microscopy imaging with the OpenFlexure Delta Stage (McDermott et al., Optics Express 2022)

name: Incubot
manufacturer: Pickering lab (University College Dublin) and colleagues

specs.Motion: entry-level 3D printer (Tronxy X1) used as the XYZ stage

summary: A live-cell microscope that sits inside a standard tissue-culture incubator, using a cheap 3D printer's motion system to move a Raspberry Pi camera and objective across the culture. A graphical interface can be modified to script experiments.

sources.title: The incubot: A 3D printer-based microscope for long-term live cell imaging within a tissue culture incubator (Merces et al., HardwareX 2021)
Full text (Europe PMC)

name: LEGO microscope
manufacturer: Vos, Blesa and Betz (University of Münster and University of Göttingen)
summary: A teaching microscope built from LEGO bricks and inexpensive lenses, with a set of experiments on biophysical principles. In a study with 9- to 13-year-old students, understanding of microscopy improved after working with it.

sources.title: Designing a High-Resolution, LEGO-Based Microscope for an Educational Setting (Vos, Blesa and Betz, The Biophysicist 2021)
bioRxiv preprint

name: smfBox
manufacturer: Craggs lab (University of Sheffield) and colleagues

specs.Lasers: 515 nm and 638 nm, alternated at 20 kHz
specs.Body: machined light-tight aluminium box replacing a microscope body

summary: An open-source confocal instrument for single-molecule FRET on freely diffusing molecules, with build instructions, acquisition software and validation published so non-specialist labs can measure distances within biomolecules.

sources.title: The smfBox is an open-source platform for single-molecule FRET (Ambrose et al., Nat. Commun. 2020)
Full text (Europe PMC)

name: Miniaturized cost-efficient localization microscope
summary: A compact localization microscope assembled from inexpensive parts that resolves cellular nanostructures below the diffraction limit. The authors propose it for practical courses that train students in super-resolution microscopy.

sources.title: A Blueprint for Cost-Efficient Localization Microscopy (Holm et al., ChemPhysChem 2014)

name: Low-cost SMLM setup

specs.Total cost: about $4,000 (vs >$100,000 for a standard SMLM set-up, per the authors)

summary: A localization microscope in which the laser, objective and camera were replaced by low-cost alternatives. Simulations and cell experiments gave localization precision and resolution similar to a standard set-up.
applications: Routine super-resolution imaging in individual labs

sources.title: A simple and cost-effective setup for super-resolution localization microscopy (Ma et al., Sci. Rep. 2017)
Full text (Europe PMC)

name: OpenSpinMicroscopy (OpenSPIN / OPenT)

specs.Modes: SPIM/DSLM light sheet or optical projection tomography (OPT)

summary: An open platform for building light-sheet (SPIM or digitally scanned) and optical projection tomography microscopes, controlled from one Micro-Manager plugin. A simpler OPT-only version, OPenT, is also documented.

sources.title: OpenSpinMicroscopy: an open-source integrated microscopy platform (Gualda et al., Nat. Methods 2013)
OpenSpin Microscopy and OPenT project site

name: openSIM

resolution.note: Bead PSF width 169 nm after SIM reconstruction vs 294 nm widefield

specs.Pattern generation: LCOS spatial light modulator illuminated by high-power LEDs
specs.Integration: replaces tube lens and illumination port adapter on commercial microscopes (e.g. Olympus, Zeiss, Leica)

summary: An open-hardware add-on that converts an existing widefield microscope into a 2D structured illumination super-resolution microscope, documented so other labs can copy it.

sources.title: Open-source microscope add-on for structured illumination microscopy (Hannebelle et al., Nat. Commun. 2024)
Full text (Europe PMC)

manufacturer: Ewers lab (Freie Universität Berlin) and openUC2
summary: A fluorescence microscope assembled from the UC2 cube toolbox around one high-quality objective, with integrated electronics and software. It reached single-molecule sensitivity for tracking and dSTORM and ran inside an incubator for multi-day live-cell imaging.

sources.title: An open-source, high-resolution, automated fluorescence microscope (Zehrer et al., eLife 2024)
Full text (Europe PMC)

specs.Connectivity: Wi-Fi access point for remote operation
